To avoid overpaying, **estimate the gas limit and check the current gas price before sending**. Don’t set an arbitrarily high limit: Pharos’s [Gas Model](/getting-started/gas-model) says fees are charged based on the gas limit at inclusion, and gas refunds don’t reduce that charge.

With Foundry, estimate the transaction and check the current price:

```bash
cast estimate <recipient> --value 0.1ether --rpc-url $RPC
cast gas-price --rpc-url $RPC
```

For a contract call, estimate using the contract address and method instead. Set the limit a little above the estimate so the transaction has room to execute, but avoid a large buffer. The Pharos guide gives **20%** as an example buffer; for cost control, don’t add more than needed.

Pharos supports EIP-1559 fees, with a dynamic base fee and a priority fee. Your wallet or library can populate those values; review them before confirming. See [Gas Model](/getting-started/gas-model) and the [Pharos Skill Engine](/tooling-and-infrastructure/pharos-skill-engine-guide) for estimation commands.
